title: Customer Network: Privacy-Preserving Audit Summaries (PRD draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working PRD sketch for a new feature: generate compact, privacy-preserving audit summaries for customer-managed networking (VPC/on-prem) changes and approval flows. Goal is to give both operators and customers enough forensic signal to investigate incidents while minimizing sensitive data surface and retention costs.

Problem statement:
- Customers want readable evidence about network/approval events (who requested change, what changed, approval path, result) but many fields contain customer IPs, internal hostnames, and ACLs that are sensitive or regulated.
- Current audit logs are full-fidelity and large; storing/retaining them long-term for all customers is costly and risky.
- Security teams require quick triage artifacts that are short, queryable, and non-sensitive by default.

Goals (MUST):
- Define a pipeline that derives "audit summaries": compact artifacts (~1-5KB) per change that contain structured, non-sensitive assertions + cryptographic attestations linking back to full logs stored in customer-controlled storage when available.
- Provide configurable privacy modes: "redact-by-default", "minimize-and-hash", and "full-trace" (enterprise opt-in).
- Integrate summaries into approval-gate UI and incident runbooks (searchable in Console).
- Retention presets: 90 days (default), 1 year (enterprise), and customer-controlled via Private deployment.

Non-goals (for this PRD):
- Replacing all full-fidelity log retention; we assume full logs live in customer S3/Logforwarder or our long-term archive when agreed.
- Solving legal/regulatory classification across jurisdictions — we will provide knobs and docs.

User stories:
- As a platform operator, I want to see a short evidence card for a VPC change so I can decide whether to approve rollback without reading raw logs.
- As a security engineer at a customer, I want Redwoods' summary artifacts to exclude internal hostnames unless I explicitly opt-in.
- As an SRE, I want the ability to query summaries by approval-id, requester, or decision-flag and jump to full logs when permitted.

High-level design:
1) Ingestion: Approval and network-change events flow through the existing control-plane event bus. Events annotated with metadata (approval-id, user-id, tenant-id, timestamp, change-delta).
2) Summarizer service (new microservice): subscribes to event bus, pulls minimal context (diff, policy hits, approver chain), and runs sanitization rules per customer privacy mode. Outputs a compact JSON summary plus a digital signature (service-key) and a pointer to the raw evidence bundle (if available).
3) Storage: summaries stored in our fast index DB (encrypted at rest) and optionally forwarded to customer-managed storage. Full raw evidence follows existing retention pipeline or customer sidecar.
4) Console/Operator UX: Summary cards embedded in the approval timeline with query links ("Show summary", "Request full evidence").

Sanitization rules (principles):
- Redact-by-default: strip IPs/hostnames, keep hashed fingerprints (sha256 truncated to 12 chars) so correlations are possible without revealing raw identifiers.
- Minimize-and-hash: include derived labels ("db-tier", "edge-nat") guessed via classifier + hashed resource ids for light traceability.
- Full-trace: include everything (for enterprise agreements).
- Always include non-sensitive metadata: approval-id, policy-id, decision, approver chain (names/ids), latency, and any policy rejections with normalized codes.

Approval gate integration:
- When a request hits an approval gate, the summarizer emits a "pre-approval summary" that shows the expected delta and any policy signals. Approver sees summary and a confidence score (0-100) for classifier labels.
- If approver selects "Require full evidence", we escalate to fetching raw logs and attach to the approval record (audit-only path).

Privacy-preserving attestations:
- Each summary carries a signature and a digest of the raw bundle (when available). This enables later forensic verification: the raw bundle can be checked against the digest to prove the summary did not mutate the original.
- For customer-managed storage, we include an optional customer-signed pointer (manual onboarding step).

Retention and cost model:
- Default behavior: store summary artifacts for 90 days in primary index (fast query).
- Archive: summaries older than 90 days moved to compressed cold storage for 1 year (searchable with higher latency).
- Enterprise: extend to 3+ years if contract.
- Cost reduction levers: adjustable sampling (1:1, 1:10) for low-risk tenants; policy-based retention (e.g., retain full evidence only when policy severity >= high).

Search & tracing UX:
- Query fields: approval-id, requester-id (or hashed requester token), policy-code, time-range, decision, resource-labels.
- Click-through from summary -> "Request raw" triggers a workflow: checks permissions (entitlement, contract), then either provides link to customer-bucket or queues a retrieval job to our archive.

Acceptance criteria (v0):
- Summarizer service can emit sanitized summaries for 3 sample change types (VPC rule change, NAT allocation, firewall update).
- Console shows summary card in approval timeline for every new request.
- Search returns summaries by approval-id within 2s for typical 30-day window.
- Privacy modes implemented: redact-by-default and full-trace. Minimize-as-hash is optional but stubbed.

Metrics and SLOs:
- Generation latency: summary produced < 5s after approval event (95th percentile).
- Query latency SLO: < 500ms for recent summaries.
- Storage SLO: summaries encrypted with KMS; keys rotated per standard practice.
- Accuracy for label classifier: baseline 80% for resource labels (measured on pilot corpus).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to handle correlated multi-change transactions (a single UI flow that makes N changes) — do we emit one summary or many? Proposal: one top-level transaction summary + N child entries.
- Legal/regulatory: are hashed fingerprints reversible in some jurisdictions? Need legal review.
- Sampling: risk of missing critical signal if sampling enabled. Need policy to force capture on high-severity changes.

Security & compliance notes:
- Summaries must be treated as audit evidence and included in incident timelines. They are not a replacement for legal subpoenas to access raw logs.
- Ensure access controls: only identities with "audit-read" can request raw evidence; summaries may be wider audience but still RBAC-protected per tenant.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (spike): build summarizer prototype, 3 sample rules, local sanitizer. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1: service + index + Console integration + basic privacy modes + tests. Pilot with 2 customers. (3 sprints)
- Phase 2: add enterprise modes, customer-managed pointers, signature verification, retention policies. (2-3 sprints)

Dependencies:
- Event bus schema stabilization (platform eng).
- KMS and signing keys (security).
- Console time-series/search integration (console team).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: summaries could leak data if sanitization rules incomplete. Mitigation: conservative redact-by-default and audit fuzz testing.
- Risk: additional storage/index cost. Mitigation: sampling and cold archive tiers.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [Priya] schedule review with legal for fingerprint/hash policy (by 2026-03-20).
- [Ethan] prototype sanitizer & classifier (spike due end of sprint).
- [Maya] design Console summary card (mockups).
- Create pilot acceptance test corpus (sample change events from engineering + anonymized customer data).

Notes and references:
- Related PRDs and experiments: PD-412 (linked), compact-evidence-serializer experiments.
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-audit (links to sample logs).

End of draft — this is intentionally high-level; expect follow-ups with concrete JSON schema for summaries and sanitized field list.
